title: House of Valois-Anjou
capsule: The House of Valois-Anjou was a cadet branch of the French royal House of Valois, established in 1356 when King John II of France created his son Louis as Duke of Anjou, subsequently also claiming the County of Provence and, from 1382, the Kingdom of Naples through the bequest of the Neapolitan queen Joanna I. Louis I, II, and III all led expensive and ultimately unsuccessful military campaigns to enforce their Neapolitan claim against the Aragonese; René of Anjou (r. 1434–1480), the dynasty's most culturally distinguished member, was definitively expelled from Naples in 1442 by Alfonso V of Aragon. The male line expired with Charles IV of Anjou in 1481, when Anjou and Provence reverted to the French Crown under Louis XI.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial holdings of this dynasty are well documented through French royal records and Provençal chancery archives; the atlas window 1363–1487 captures the period from the duchy's creation to just before the final reversion to the Crown.
